One-sentence judgment: secondary school career and technical education teachers are not about "finishing the textbook"; they teach the knowledge and skills of an occupational or technical field to adolescents at the secondary stage, and are accountable for course objectives, practicum safety, student records, and assessment quality. O*NET classifies this occupation as Job Zone Four (considerable preparation, SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), does not mark it Bright Outlook, and gives an interest code of SCA (Social, Conventional, Artistic). The core boundary: the teaching credential, the subject taught, and the stage taught must each be obtained under local rules, and student assessment and promotion decisions, the handling and reporting of student protection matters, and the conditions under which practicum equipment may be operated are all different responsibilities, so a teacher may not overstep to replace the school or the competent authority in handling them.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to explain the same thing repeatedly to students with different foundations and adjust your approach, and can attend to learning progress and personal safety at the same time in the classroom and at the practicum site (the O*NET work context shows that among 100 interest codes Social is the highest, 94 for the work activity of teaching and instructing others, 82% in continuous contact with others, 73% making public speeches every day, and 80% working more than 40 hours per week); you are willing to record student performance and attendance and assessment evidence truthfully and completely, accept working to curriculum standards and school systems, and report per procedures when a student shows an abnormality or is suspected of being harmed rather than handling it on your own.

Conditions for pausing major investment first: you have not yet completed one full closed loop from setting course objectives and lesson plans and practicum safety plans and assessment design through recording and communication; or you are unwilling to record and report truthfully per the system, unwilling to emphasize safety procedures repeatedly during practicum, and unwilling to face questions from parents and colleagues; also, do not treat knowing a trade or having worked in the industry as proof that you already have classroom management and student guidance ability.

Education, credentials, and authorization must be checked separately: O*NET classifies this occupation as Job Zone Four (considerable preparation, SVP 7.0 to below 8.0), and the O*NET education survey shows 40% of respondents consider a bachelor's degree necessary, 23% a master's degree, and 13% an associate or other two-year degree; the occupation page lists 1 apprenticeship direction (Agriculture Education Instructor) and 9 certifications (including National Board Certification - Career & Technical Education, Praxis Subject Assessment, Microsoft Certified Educator, and Certified in Family and Consumer Sciences). In mainland China, teaching requires obtaining the teacher credential for the corresponding stage and subject under the teacher credential system, and meeting the school's recruitment and employment conditions; a teacher credential does not equal employment, the range of stages and subjects taught, authorization as a class adviser or practicum supervisor, or the school's approval to offer a specific practicum program.

In one sentence: this is a role that turns "has this occupational or technical course actually been learned by the students, and is the process safe and traceable" into reviewable evidence; the outputs are course objectives and lesson plans, classroom and practicum records, student assessment and grading evidence, student performance and attendance records, practicum safety and equipment inspection records, and communication records with students, parents, and colleagues; it is not the school management and curriculum approval role, nor does it replace the school's or the competent authority's handling and reporting of student protection matters. This page does not publish occupation-level wage figures for mainland China and only registers the scope and gaps with visible markers.

The work of this occupation falls into three categories: first, classroom teaching (setting course objectives and lesson plans, lecturing, demonstrating, and discussing, assigning and grading homework and tests, assessing student progress, and adjusting the pace to the curriculum standards); second, practicum and safety instruction (preparing and maintaining practicum equipment and materials, demonstrating and supervising equipment use and care, checking the site and equipment for hazards, and establishing and enforcing order and safety procedures in the classroom and practicum site); third, recording and communication (maintaining student enrollment and performance and attendance and assessment records, communicating with parents or guardians and colleagues and administrators, participating in individualized support and tutoring and job placement referrals, and reporting abnormalities per procedures). All three share the same chain built around course objectives, evidence of student learning, and traceable records.
Classroom teaching

Set course and unit objectives → prepare lesson plans and teaching materials → lecture, demonstrate, and run group practice → assign and grade homework and tests → adjust the pace and provide individualized tutoring based on assessment results → record teaching and student progress
Practicum and safety instruction

Editorial practicum process: check the equipment and site protection before class, and demonstrate and supervise safe student use; Article 18 of China's school safety measures requires hazardous facilities to be taken out of service and repaired, replaced, protected, or marked promptly, with the specific decommissioning and restoration following school rules, and the page does not specify teacher repair authority.

Collect evidence of student performance and attendance and assessment → grade to standards and state the basis → maintain enrollment and grade and communication records → communicate progress and improvement points with students and parents or guardians → collaborate with colleagues and counselors and administrators on individual needs → report abnormalities per procedures and keep records

Secondary school career and technical education teachers have as their core output course objectives, evidence of student learning, and traceable records; training and development specialists focus on improving the job competence of incumbent workers, educational guidance and career counselors focus on students' further education and career counseling, and business teachers, computer science teachers, and family and consumer sciences teachers teach and research a subject at the higher education stage, while instructional coordinators coordinate curriculum and instruction and train teachers. Similar names or being in the same education chain do not mean that the teaching credential, the scope of teaching, assessment authority, and authority to handle student protection matters are interchangeable.
Core purpose

Let secondary students truly acquire verifiable knowledge and skills in an occupational or technical field and complete practicum safely: ensure teaching has a basis through course objectives and lesson plans, make learning visible and reviewable through assessment and records, and keep the process controllable through safety procedures and order management.
Main objects and basis

The objects are secondary stage students and classes and practicum groups, as well as curriculum standards and textbooks and lesson plans, practicum equipment and tools and materials and protective equipment, classrooms and laboratories and workshop sites, tests and homework and assessment standards, enrollment and grade and attendance and communication records, and individualized support and tutoring and job placement and extracurricular activity arrangements; the basis is the local teacher credential and scope of teaching rules, school and district policies and administrative regulations, curriculum standards and syllabi, practicum safety and equipment operation and site management rules, student record and privacy and mandatory reporting requirements, and the school's approval system for courses and activities.
Core process

Setting course objectives, preparing lesson plans and materials, lecturing and demonstrating, organizing practicum and patrolling for safety, assigning and grading homework and tests, assessing and recording student progress, communicating with parents and colleagues, and reporting abnormalities per procedures and completing records.
Main outputs

Course objectives and lesson plans and teaching materials, classroom and practicum records, test and homework and assessment results and grading evidence, student performance and attendance and enrollment records, practicum equipment and site inspection and maintenance records, communication records with students and parents or guardians, individualized support and tutoring and job placement and referral records, and abnormality and reporting records.
Accountable party

Teachers are responsible for teaching, assessment, and on-site instruction per the division of labor, and schools implement the principal responsibility system under Article 16 of the safety measures; the statutory reporting duty for student protection is borne directly by the relevant staff. Article 11 of China's Law on the Protection of Minors requires units and staff in close contact with minors to report immediately to public security, civil affairs, education, and other relevant departments when they discover abuse, suspected abuse, or other danger; internal school reporting cannot substitute for or delay the statutory report, and immediate danger requires prompt rescue without waiting for internal approval.
Authority and approval

Article 11 of China's Teachers Law distinguishes junior secondary (college or above) from senior secondary / secondary vocational cultural and specialized courses (bachelor's or above); secondary vocational practicum supervision is, under Article 7 of the implementation measures, secondary vocational graduation or above, and under Article 7 of the regulations requires assistant engineer or above or intermediate worker grade or above, with a reduction in education requirements for special skills subject to approval. Article 5 of the credential regulations makes senior secondary and secondary vocational teacher credentials mutually recognized, with additional limits on the applicability of the practicum supervision credential; a credential does not equal school employment or authority over all courses. 
Hazardous facilities are to be taken out of service and reported under the law; student danger requires prompt rescue and reporting, and one cannot wait for course approval first.
Conclusion boundaries

Course records and assessment results state "how students performed under the given curriculum standards, class conditions, and teaching conditions"; they are not a final characterization of a student's ability, nor do they replace the school's and competent authority's handling of student protection matters, and they are updated as curriculum standards, class composition, and teaching arrangements change; when citing them, state the curriculum standard version, the assessment method, and the record period as well.

Before starting, check at least six items: job duties (career and technical course teaching, practicum and equipment safety instruction, student guidance and further education and employment counseling, curriculum and program design, or instructional coordination), the required teacher credential and the stage and subject scope taught, practicum site and equipment conditions and the division of safety responsibility, class size and teaching hours and workload arrangements, student record and communication and mandatory reporting requirements, and whether you are responsible for class adviser duties or extracurricular activities or school-enterprise cooperation.
Occupation scope

This frozen identity is 25-2032.00 secondary school CTE teachers, sharing a SOC with 0143 but retaining an independent asset. O*NET Job Zone4, not marked Bright Outlook, with educational services 99% and other 1%. O*NET interest SCA: S100/C49/A41/I40/R31/E25; the specific interests of teaching 99, social service 72, professional counseling 69, and public speaking 60 are separate dimensions, not S sub-scores or a personal competence threshold. Related secondary vocational and senior secondary courses in China can be compared for duties, but no one-to-one occupation wage mapping has been established.
Education and training paths

The O*NET entry-level education survey shows 40% bachelor's, 23% master's, and 13% associate, which is not the incumbent education composition; Job Zone4 is a cross-occupation preparation zone, and the 1 Agriculture Education Instructor apprenticeship example does not prove current enrollment or a requirement for everyone. 
The U.S. BLS summarizes the common pattern of a bachelor's degree plus work experience in the field taught; state credential/licensure conditions for public schools vary by state, and the teaching internship, background check, and examinations must be checked on the specific route, with the 9 linked certifications and examinations not all being state licenses or required across all occupations. 
Article 11 of China's Teachers Law distinguishes junior secondary (college or above) from senior secondary / secondary vocational cultural and specialized courses (bachelor's or above); secondary vocational practicum supervision is, under Article 7 of the implementation measures, secondary vocational graduation or above, and under Article 7 of the regulations requires assistant engineer or above or intermediate worker grade or above, with a reduction in education requirements for special skills subject to approval. Article 5 of the credential regulations makes senior secondary and secondary vocational teacher credentials mutually recognized, with additional limits on the applicability of the practicum supervision credential; a credential does not equal school employment or authority over all courses.
Methods and tools

The O*NET technology list gives 12 software skill categories, and the Hot Technologies page lists 7 (Autodesk AutoCAD Civil 3D, Google Docs, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Office software, Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft PowerPoint, and Microsoft Word), with no individual proportions given on that page (data source: Lightcast 2025 U.S. job postings). On-site methods and tools are mainly practicum equipment and tools and protective equipment, classroom lecturing and demonstration equipment, learning management systems and grade and attendance recording systems, testing and homework and assessment tools, curriculum standards and textbooks and lesson plan materials, and channels for communicating with parents. Job posting demand labels indicate frequency of appearance in employer job advertisements and do not mean the institution has deployed such tools or that the position has been replaced.
Safety and work permits

The work is mainly a fixed in-school timetable with office hours, plus after-hours workload such as lesson preparation, grading, and communication; the main demands come from long periods of standing and speaking, continuous interpersonal interaction and emotional labor, and watching over several students' safety at the same time at the practicum site. The O*NET work context shows: 82% in continuous contact with others; 80% working more than 40 hours per week; 73% making public speeches every day; 67% having face-to-face discussions every day; 59% making decisions every day that affect others, organizational resources, or reputation; 55% indoors environmentally controlled every day; 51% dealing with unpleasant, angry, or discourteous people at least once a week; 51% considering coordinating or leading others extremely important; 48% working at moderate physical proximity to others (within arm's reach); 43% reporting a lot of freedom over tasks and priorities; 39% having extremely high responsibility for the health and safety of others; 38% reporting a lot of decision freedom; 38% standing about half the time; 33% exposed daily to distracting or uncomfortable noise. Operations must follow curriculum standards and school systems, and practicum must implement protection and patrol per equipment and site safety procedures, with student safety protected first and then reported when a student safety abnormality is found. 
The above are U.S. respondent contexts; internal school systems cannot replace China's statutory reporting. Article 11 of China's Law on the Protection of Minors requires units and staff in close contact with minors to report immediately to public security, civil affairs, education, and other relevant departments when they discover infringements of minors' rights and interests, suspected infringements, or other danger; internal school reporting cannot substitute for or delay the statutory report, and immediate danger requires prompt rescue without waiting for internal approval.
Training and regulatory requirements

The U.S. BLS summarizes the common pattern of a bachelor's degree plus work experience in the field taught; state credential/licensure conditions for public schools vary by state, and the teaching internship, background check, and examinations must be checked on the specific route, with the 9 linked certifications and examinations not all being state licenses or required across all occupations. 
Article 11 of China's Teachers Law distinguishes junior secondary (college or above) from senior secondary / secondary vocational cultural and specialized courses (bachelor's or above); secondary vocational practicum supervision is, under Article 7 of the implementation measures, secondary vocational graduation or above, and under Article 7 of the regulations requires assistant engineer or above or intermediate worker grade or above, with a reduction in education requirements for special skills subject to approval. Article 5 of the credential regulations makes senior secondary and secondary vocational teacher credentials mutually recognized, with additional limits on the applicability of the practicum supervision credential; a credential does not equal school employment or authority over all courses.
Pay and hours

U.S. secondary CTE teachers usually follow the school timetable, but lesson preparation and home-school communication happen before and after class; O*NET80% work more than 40 hours per week, and the traditional academic-year holiday is not a uniformly mandated arrangement in all schools. The 2025 U.S. median annual wage is 66,270 USD, annual percentile only. U.S. 25-2032 secondary school career and technical education teachers: employment 110,500 in 2025 and 110,100 projected in 2035; the 2025—2035 change rate is 0% (rounded, Little or no change), a net change of about -400, and 6,400 average annual openings (growth and replacement demand, not net new additions). 
The National Bureau of Statistics 2025 education industry gives 133,539 yuan for urban non-private units and 63,908 yuan for private units, both pre-tax annual averages and multi-occupation industry references; they are not this occupation's average, median, starting pay, or monthly salary. Specific teaching hours, establishment, holidays, and contract pay are checked separately.

Secondary school career and technical education teachers (O*NET-SOC 25-2032.00) teach career, vocational, career-exploration, or technical subjects to students at the secondary stage. Daily work includes: using various teaching methods such as lecture, discussion, and demonstration to instruct students individually and in groups; establishing and enforcing behavioral rules and procedures that maintain student order; preparing materials and the classroom for class activities; observing and evaluating students' performance, behavior, social development, and physical health; teaching the knowledge and skills required for a specific occupation or occupational field under a systematic plan of lectures, discussions, audiovisual presentations, and laboratory, workshop, and on-site learning; instructing and supervising students in the use and care of equipment and materials to prevent injury and damage; setting clear objectives for all lessons, units, and projects and communicating them to students; using computers, audiovisual aids, and other equipment and materials to supplement presentations; instructing and counseling students with adjustment or academic problems or special academic interests; maintaining accurate and complete student records as required by law, district policy, and administrative regulations; planning and conducting a balanced program of instruction, demonstration, and work time so that students have opportunities to observe, question, and investigate; preparing, administering, and grading tests and assignments to evaluate student progress; assigning and grading class work and homework; enforcing all administration policies and rules governing students; providing assistive devices, supportive technology, and assistance accessing facilities for students with disabilities; preparing students for later grades by encouraging them to explore learning opportunities and persevere with challenging tasks; planning and supervising class projects, field trips, guest speakers, and other experiential activities and guiding students in learning from them; conferring with parents or guardians, other teachers, counselors, and administrators to resolve students' behavioral and academic problems; keeping informed about trends in education and the subject field taught; planning and supervising work experience programs in business, industrial workshops, and school laboratories; meeting with other professionals to discuss individual students' needs and progress; preparing and implementing remedial programs for students requiring extra help; establishing course objectives and outlines per curriculum guidelines or state and school requirements; meeting with parents or guardians to discuss their children's progress and to determine priorities and resource needs; arranging for students to gain work placements or referring them to job placement services; selecting, ordering, storing, issuing, and inventorying classroom equipment, materials, and supplies; advising student clubs, student organizations, academic competitions, and other extracurricular activities; collaborating with other teachers and administrators to develop, evaluate, and revise secondary school curriculum programs; attending professional meetings, educational conferences, and teacher training workshops to maintain and improve professional competence; meeting with other staff to plan and schedule courses according to the approved curriculum; preparing reports on students and activities as required by administration; and attending staff meetings and serving on committees as required, along with administrative duties such as library assistance, hall and cafeteria duty, and bus loading and unloading supervision. It carries responsibility for student protection, teaching quality, and the scope of teaching, but does not replace the school's and competent authority's responsibility for curriculum approval, handling student protection matters, and personnel management.

paragraphs: This page compares secondary school career and technical education teachers with six adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference is better suited to. Adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupation descriptions and do not mean the job titles or teaching credentials are interchangeable.

Evidence note: the career direction and core outputs are based on O*NET-SOC 25-2032.00 and the official descriptions of the adjacent entries (U.S. scope); the adjacent occupations listed by this evidence route are training and development specialists, educational guidance and career counselors, business teachers (postsecondary), computer science teachers (postsecondary), and family and consumer sciences teachers (postsecondary), with instructional coordinators being an O*NET related occupation; teacher credentials and scope of teaching, student assessment and promotion decisions, and authority to handle and report student protection matters must be verified separately for each jurisdiction and school system, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut for changing careers.

The table below compares the differences in duties and outputs between secondary school career and technical education teachers and the adjacent directions; the basis for judging is the main outputs, what the work is accountable for, and the required qualifications, not how similar the job titles are.

Training and development specialists design and deliver in-service training inside organizations and are employed by companies and institutions; this occupation works with adolescent students at the secondary stage and is bound by curriculum standards and teacher credentials and school systems.

If you would rather train and upskill incumbent workers, look first at the training and development specialist direction; if you would rather teach career and technical courses in a secondary classroom, look first at this occupation.
Improving job competence for incumbent workers, with output mainly training plans and training effectiveness evaluation.
Training and Development Specialists

Educational guidance and career counselors mainly use individual and group counseling and work directly on students' further education and career choices; this occupation centers on course teaching and assessment, with student guidance only one part of the duties.

If you would rather do further education and career counseling and individual guidance, look first at the educational guidance and career counselor direction; if you would rather carry course teaching and assessment responsibility, look first at this occupation.
Provide further education and career counseling and individual guidance, with output mainly counseling records and individualized plans.
Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors

Business teachers (postsecondary) usually need an advanced degree in the discipline and carry research and academic publication requirements, teaching college and graduate students; this occupation teaches secondary students, with a focus on career and technical skills and practicum safety.

If you would rather teach and research a discipline in higher education, look first at the business teacher (postsecondary) direction (usually requiring a higher degree); if you would rather do career and technical education in a secondary school, look first at this occupation.
Teach business courses and conduct research at the higher education stage, with output mainly course teaching and academic output.
Business Teachers, Postsecondary

Computer science teachers (postsecondary) carry disciplinary research and student research supervision, teaching college and graduate students; this occupation works on secondary stage technical courses and practicum and does not carry disciplinary research duties.

If you would rather do teaching and research in computer science in higher education, look first at the computer science teacher (postsecondary) direction; if you would rather teach technical courses to secondary students, look first at this occupation.
Teach computer science courses and conduct research at the higher education stage, with output mainly course teaching and academic output.
Computer Science Teachers, Postsecondary

Family and consumer sciences teachers (postsecondary) center on disciplinary courses and research, teaching college and graduate students; this occupation teaches secondary students career and technical courses in the corresponding field and is responsible for practicum safety.

If you would rather do teaching and research in this field in higher education, look first at the family and consumer sciences teacher (postsecondary) direction; if you would rather teach related career courses in a secondary school, look first at this occupation.
Teach family and consumer sciences courses and conduct research at the higher education stage, with output mainly course teaching and academic output.
Family and Consumer Sciences Teachers, Postsecondary

Instructional coordinators coordinate and guide the curriculum system and the teacher group and do not carry day-to-day class teaching and assessment responsibility; this occupation works directly with students and carries classroom teaching and practicum safety and assessment responsibility.

If you would rather coordinate curriculum and instruction and train teachers, look first at the instructional coordinator direction; if you would rather work directly with students and carry teaching and assessment responsibility, look first at this occupation.

entries.answer: Teach career and vocational skills and career or technical subjects at the secondary stage: use methods such as lecture, discussion, and demonstration to instruct students individually and in groups; establish and enforce behavioral rules and procedures that maintain order; prepare materials and the classroom for class activities; observe and evaluate students' performance and behavior and social development and physical health; teach the knowledge and skills required for a specific occupational field under a systematic plan; instruct and supervise students in the use and care of equipment and materials to prevent injury and damage; set clear objectives for courses and units and projects and communicate them to students; prepare, administer, and grade tests and assignments; assign and grade class work and homework; provide assistive devices and supportive technology and assistance accessing facilities for students with disabilities; confer with parents or guardians and other teachers and counselors and administrators to resolve students' behavioral and academic problems; plan and supervise class projects and field trips and work experience programs; maintain student records as required by law and district policy; advise student clubs and extracurricular activities; and attend teaching group work and training and staff meetings.

entries.answer: The main risks are student injury from insufficient practicum supervision, privacy consequences from improper handling of student records and family information, unfair or inaccurate assessment and grade handling, practicum equipment and site hazards not being removed promptly, handling student protection matters beyond authority or delaying a report, and competence depreciation under curriculum standard and technical updates; control depends on pre-class equipment and site checks, continuous patrol and correction during student operation, maintaining and accessing student records per the system, grading to published standards with retained evidence, protecting the student first and reporting per procedures when harm is suspected, and continuous participation in teaching group work and training.
entries.question: What risks does this job most require you to watch out for in advance?

entries.answer: Fit signals are being able to adjust the approach for students with different foundations and maintain classroom order, being willing to patrol the practicum site continuously and correct unsafe behavior, and being able to report per procedures rather than handling it yourself when a student shows an abnormality; what matters is whether there are reviewable lesson plans and classroom records, assessment and grading evidence, student records, and actual teaching performance, not just an interest in a craft or industry experience.

entries.answer: Course objectives and teaching judgments, evaluation of student performance and behavior, assessment standards and grade determination and changes, promotion and referral recommendations, practicum on-site safety judgments and decisions to suspend use, the recording and time limits for student records and reporting, and checking the consistency of automatic grading results with the original assignments must all be completed and documented by an authorized person.

subject.name: Career/Technical Education Teachers, Secondary School
subject.summary: This page's entry corresponds to secondary school career and technical education teachers (O*NET-SOC 25-2032.00): teaching career and vocational skills and career or technical subjects to students at the secondary stage — using lecture, discussion, and demonstration for individual and group instruction, setting course and unit objectives and preparing lesson plans and materials, establishing and enforcing behavioral rules that maintain classroom and practicum order, instructing and supervising students in the use and care of equipment to prevent injury and damage, observing and evaluating students' performance and behavior and social development and physical health, preparing and grading tests and assignments, maintaining student records as required by law and district policy, and communicating student progress with parents or guardians and colleagues; the work is mainly a fixed in-school timetable (82% in continuous contact with others, 73% making a public speech every day, 80% working more than 40 hours per week, 39% having extremely high responsibility for the health and safety of others), and its duties do not replace the school's and competent authority's responsibility for curriculum approval and personnel management, and student protection matters are handled by designated positions per the system.
